neighbours.label: Code or prose that first names a group of several items and then sets up singling out ONE of them by position or rank (first, last, eldest, lowest, [0], [-1], pop): it lights up on the word just before the pick, so a setup that reaches that slot fires even if no pick follows; mentioning a group and using it whole (counting, sorting, printing all of it) stays quiet
neighbours.short: set-up to pick the first/last one of a group
fire: Simon is the fourth from the left in the centre row.
Of the five sisters, the eldest became a doctor.
We tried three restaurants on the trip, and the last one was by far the best.
Among all the candidates who applied, the lowest bid came from a small local firm.
The team ran four laps, and on the final lap Maria finally pulled ahead.
quiet: Humans should make the best use of given information at any time.
The five sisters all gathered for dinner on Sunday.
We tried three restaurants on the trip and enjoyed every one of them.
All the candidates who applied submitted bids before the deadline.
The team ran four laps together and then stretched on the grass.

predictions: Blind test (label-only author). Expect most code fires to clear 0.20; prose fires weaker; the 'fourth from the left' fire item resembles the - pole's top examples and will likely miss.
